{{Short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=January 2025}} {{Infobox college sports team season |year=2023–24 |team=NC State Wolfpack |sport=Basketball |image=North Carolina State University Athletic logo.svg |image_size=100 |conference=Atlantic Coast Conference |division= |short_conf=ACC |record= 26–15 |conf_record= 9–11 |APRank= 10 |CoachRank= 13 |head_coach=[[Kevin Keatts]] |hc_year = 7th |asst_coach1=Joel Justus |asst_coach2=[[Kareem Richardson]] |asst_coach3=Levi Watkins |asst_coach4=Larry Dixon |stadium=[[PNC Arena]] | champion = [[2024 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] champions | tourney =[[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = Final Four }} {{2023–24 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2023–24 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team''' represented [[North Carolina State University]] during the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Wolfpack were led by seventh-year head coach [[Kevin Keatts]] and played their home games at [[PNC Arena]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). The NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team drew an average home attendance of 13,491 in 17 games in 2023-24.{{cite web |url=http://fs.ncaa.org.s3.amazonaws.com/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/Attend.pdf |title=Men's Basketball Attendance Records Through 2023-24 |page=5 |website=fs.ncaa.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250602233707/http://fs.ncaa.org.s3.amazonaws.com/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/Attend.pdf |archive-date=June 2, 2025 |url-status=live}} The Wolfpack finished the regular season on an uninspiring four-game losing streak, consequently posting a regular season record of 17–14 (9–11 in conference play) and slumping to the ACC tournament as the 10th seed. They then went on a miraculous run in the ACC tournament, winning five games in the span of five days (including a victory over ACC regular season champion and rival [[2023–24 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]) to win their first ACC tournament since [[1987 ACC men's basketball tournament|1987]]. They became the first team to win their conference tournament with five wins in five days since the [[2010–11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|2010–11 Connecticut Huskies]] (of the Big East) and the second team overall to do it since the NCAA tournament began in 1939.{{Cite web |date=2024-03-17 |title=NC State stuns North Carolina, wins ACC Tournament behind D.J. Burns Jr., DJ Horne and an unshakeable spirit |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/nc-state-stuns-north-carolina-wins-acc-tournament-behind-d-j-burns-jr-dj-horne-and-an-unshakeable-spirit/ |access-date=2025-01-16 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} This is the first time the Wolfpack made the NCAA tournament in consecutive years since they made the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2014]] and [[1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2015 tournament]]. Receiving an #11 seed in the South region of the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], they continued their [[Cinderella run]] from the ACC tournament by defeating #6 [[2023–24 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]] in the first round, #14 [[2023–24 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]] in overtime in the second round, #2 [[2023–24 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]] in the Sweet Sixteen, and their ACC rivals #4 [[2023–24 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the Elite Eight. The Wolfpack made their first Final Four appearance since [[1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1983]] as a result, having won nine straight games since the end of the regular season. They became the sixth #11 seed to reach the Final Four and the first since [[2020-21 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] in 2021. Their miraculous run came to an end with a Final Four loss to [[2023–24 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], closing their season with a 26–15 record. ==Previous season== The [[2022–23 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|Wolfpack]] finished the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]] 23–11, 12–8 in [[2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in sixth place. They defeated [[2022–23 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] before losing to [[2022–23 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] in the [[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 11 seed in the South region. There they lost to [[2022–23 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] in the first round. ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {|class="wikitable sortable" border="1" style="text-align: center;"
